title: Who to Trust in Multi-Robot Systems: Joint Robot and Object Hypothesis Trust Inference via Neural-Symbolic Cross-Validation
abstract: arXiv:2610.14530v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-robot systems (MRS) offer significant advantages over single-robot platforms by enabling information sharing and coordination for different tasks in complex environments. However, reliable cooperation critically depends on inferring trust over both information sources and their reported hypotheses, particularly under partial observability and potential adversarial interference. Existing approaches frequently depend on pre-established trust relationships or side-channel information, which may not be available or reliable in realistic MRS deployments. This work introduces NeST-Bayes, a neural-symbolic framework that jointly infers robot and hypothesis trust using only inter-robot observation consistency, without requiring preassigned robot trust, reputation information, or side-channel identity signals. translated_title: 多机器人系统中该信任谁：基于神经-符号交叉验证的机器人与目标假设联合信任推断
translated_abstract: 多机器人系统（MRS）通过在复杂环境中实现信息共享与多任务协作，相比单机器人平台具有显著优势。然而，可靠的协作关键取决于对信息源及其报告假设的信任推断，尤其是在部分可观测和存在潜在对抗性干扰的情况下。现有方法通常依赖于预先建立的信任关系或旁路信息，而这些信息在实际的多机器人系统部署中可能不可用或不可靠。本工作提出了 NeST-Bayes，这是一种神经-符号框架，仅利用机器人之间的观测一致性来联合推断机器人和假设的信任，无需预先设定的机器人信任值、声誉信息或旁路身份信号。NeST-Bayes 通过对以自我为中心的关系图进行推理，为机器人和目标假设计算瞬时信任证据分数……
tldr: 该论文提出 NeST-Bayes 神经-符号框架，仅凭机器人间的观测一致性即可联合推断机器人与目标假设的信任度，摆脱了对预置信任关系、声誉信息或旁路身份信号的依赖。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes NeST-Bayes, a neural-symbolic framework that jointly infers trust in robots and object hypotheses using only inter-robot observation consistency, eliminating the need for preassigned trust relationships, reputation information, or side-channel identity signals.
